finalText:
Root cause: Redis died, cache-less fallback overloaded store, queue grew unbounded, worker OOM, service killed.

**Note:** log dates `2026-07-04`, not last night. Either old file or clock wrong — check before you chase last night's incident.

## Timeline (all UTC)

| Time | Event |
|---|---|
| 02:00–02:14 | Healthy. 200s only, latency 12–145ms, cache hit ratio 0.90–0.98 |
| 02:14:07.113 | `ERROR [api] redis connection lost: connect ECONNREFUSED 10.0.0.12:6379` |
| 02:14:07.114 | `WARN [api] cache layer degraded — falling back to direct store reads` |
| 02:14:08 | Cache miss storm starts |
| 02:14:10 | First `TimeoutError: request timed out after 5000ms (store overloaded)` |
| 02:14:12 | Queue depth 52 |
| 02:15:26 – 02:31:26 | 13 reconnect attempts (0–12), every one `ECONNREFUSED`, never recover |
| 02:29:12 | Queue depth 502 — **passes max 500**, no shed, keeps climbing |
| 02:31:24 | Queue depth 568 |
| 02:31:44.902 | `ERROR [worker-2] JavaScript heap out of memory (request backlog)` |
| 02:31:45.001 | `FATAL [supervisor] worker-2 exited with code 134, restarting` |
| 02:31:52.318 | `FATAL [supervisor] api unresponsive, killing process group — service down` |

17m45s from Redis loss to service down.

## What actually happened

1. Redis at `10.0.0.12:6379` refused connections. ECONNREFUSED = host up, port closed. Redis process dead or restarted, not network partition. **Root cause lives on Redis box, not in this service.** Log has no Redis-side reason.
2. Fallback read straight from store. No circuit breaker.
3. Miss storm keys cycle `orders:1000`–`orders:1199` — only 200 distinct keys, repeating. Classic stampede: no single-flight/lock, so every concurrent request for same key hit store separately.
4. Store saturated, 5000ms timeouts. Queue depth grew ~1.5/s, steady, whole 17 min.
5. `max 500` was logged but never enforced. Depth passed 500 at 02:29:12, reached 568. Backlog ate heap, worker-2 OOM (exit 134 = SIGABRT), api went unresponsive, supervisor killed group.

## Fixes, ranked

1. **Enforce queue max 500.** Reject with 503 past limit. This alone stops OOM — degrade, not die.
2. **Circuit breaker on store.** After N timeouts, fail fast instead of piling 5s waits.
3. **Single-flight on cache miss.** 200 hot keys stampeding = most of store load is duplicate work.
4. **Reconnect backoff.** Attempts fixed ~80s apart, 13 tries, no jitter, no alert escalation. Minor vs above but fix it.
5. **Alert on `cache layer degraded`.** 17 minutes of warning existed and nothing paged.

No deploy or traffic spike in log. Traffic pattern flat before and after — this was pure dependency failure, not load.
